# Copilot code-review instructions

This repo is a BepInEx 6 (IL2CPP) Harmony mod for *Survival Log*. Plugins derive from `BasePlugin` and call the game through Il2CppInterop proxy assemblies. Review with these traps in mind; a general C# review misses most of them.

## IL2CPP Harmony traps

- **Getter/setter patches often never fire.** il2cpp inlines trivial accessors, so a `MethodType.Getter`/`.Setter` patch silently does nothing. Flag a new getter patch used as the only mechanism. The reliable change is mutating the backing field at a load hook.
- **No `is`/`as` across the interop boundary.** Flag `is`, `as`, or a direct cast on a game type. The correct form is `x.TryCast<T>()` then a null check.
- **No `foreach` over game collections.** The interop enumerator lacks the pattern. Expect `GetEnumerator()` / `MoveNext()` / `Current`, or a count plus an indexer.
- **Never read an `Il2CppSystem.ValueTuple<...>` result of a game method,** direct or as a list element. The interop layer reads the fields wrongly and gives garbage with no error. Expect a method that returns a class, a dictionary, or an `Il2CppStructArray`, or the value calculated in the mod.
- **Guard game lookups.** Singletons and config lookups return null often. Flag an unchecked dereference inside a patch.
- **A patch must not break the game.** Each patch body sits in a try/catch that logs the error, so the HUD and the action queue fall back to the game's own behavior.
- **A robot patch checks its switch first.** Each patch of the robot groups and both native detours attach at the start, and their first statement checks `EnableRobotReplant` (a Prefix returns `true`, a Postfix returns, a detour calls the original), so the switch takes effect while the game runs; the library `config-file` reads a hand edit of the file at a save load or the settings window open. Flag robot work before the switch check.

## Structure and tests

- **Feature folders.** Each feature has its own folder under `src/` (`Grid/`, `Hover/`, `Patrol/`, `Replant/`, `Robot/`, `PotOptions/`, `Web/`) with its patches, its game-facing code, and its game-free `*Logic.cs` file. `Plugin.cs` holds only the config, the patch list, and the per-frame tick. Flag a new patch that is not in the patch list of `Plugin.Load`: each patch class is attached on its own, so a target missing after a game update turns off only its feature.
- **Pure logic is separated and tested.** Logic that does not need the running game (the grid layout by floor and climate area, the area value texts of `AreaFormat`, the send decisions of `SendLogic`, the badges, the hover rules, the Patrol chores and route, the robot preset rules, the replant decision, the fertilizer choice, the save keys, the page JSON, the opacity rule) lives in the `*Logic.cs` files, `src/Grid/AreaFormat.cs`, `src/Web/SendLogic.cs`, `src/Web/PageJson.cs`, and `src/Web/PageStyle.cs`, with no BepInEx or Il2Cpp reference, unit-tested under `tests/Greenline.Tests`. Flag new pure logic in a game-facing file, and new pure logic with no test. The route order and the walk length come from the library copy `src/Shared/route/`, the floor lines and zone lines from `src/Shared/floor-grid/`, and the pin from `src/Shared/hud-pin/` (with `src/Shared/json/` and `src/Shared/i18n/`): each copy is written by a sync from the modding workspace and never edited here, so flag a hand edit of a file under `src/Shared/`.
- **Patches** prefer a postfix, and tie the `Harmony` instance to the plugin GUID. A Prefix returns `false` only in the mod's own case: the mod's own page messages (`GREENLINE_POT_OPTION`, `GREENLINE_TEND`, `GREENLINE_REPLANT`, `GREENLINE_PIN`, and the `slmod|greenline|` messages of `PageMessages`), and the Same as last crop placeholder of a robot sowing preset. The plan of a robot sow goes through a native detour of `PlantChoreManager.ResolveSowPlan` (`RobotPlanDetour`), not Harmony: flag a Harmony patch of a method with a struct argument by reference, and any hook of `RobotSowRules.GetPreset` (it crashed the game).
- **Native detours.** A second detour of `PlantChoreManager.TryResolveChore` (`RobotOrderDetour` in `src/Robot/RobotOrder.cs`) sets the chore order of a robot: only after the original returns true, and only for a Till (1618) or a robot Plant (9130) candidate, it writes `Rank` and `DecayRemain` from `RobotLogic.FinishRank`; each other chore stays as the game wrote it. Its native delegate returns a `byte`, not a `bool`, because il2cpp gives a C# `bool` in the low byte only; flag a `bool` return in a native delegate. The struct field offsets of each detour come from the il2cpp metadata at load (`NativeMeta.FieldOffset`, by field name and type, less the object header), never from a hard-coded number. Each detour has its own patch group in `Plugin.cs` (`PatchRobot` for Same as last crop, `PatchRobotOrder` for the order, both attached only when `EnableRobotReplant` is on), so a missing target turns off only its own feature with one warning; flag a detour added to another feature's group.
- **Normal game actions only.** Tend All is Greenline's own Patrol: it queues each chore as a click in the menu of the pot does, through the game's own request, so the game checks and runs it as such. The label of the Tend All button is the mod's own text ("Tend All", 一键巡田), not the game's text key `SR_Web_CoreUI1_117`, which game 1.1.19611 gave to its own Patrol (Tend Garden, 巡园). The game's own Patrol stays off while `EnablePatrol` is on: `GamePatrolOff` sets `GameKey.PlantChoreBatchEnabled` to false before `Reducer_Web_CoreUI1.RA_PlantOverviewUnlock` reads it, and that one switch gates its button, the hotkey G, the quick action, and the guide tip. Flag code that turns the game's own Patrol on, or leaves it on while `EnablePatrol` is on. The replant plants through the game's own planting action, with the normal Stamina cost and the seeds and fertilizer from the same containers as the planting window. Flag code that gives items, crops, or EXP directly, skips a Stamina cost, or changes a Plant chore that the player started by hand.
- **The fertilizer pick follows the game's part dose.** The game plants with `min(have, pot size)` of the chosen fertilizer and gives its speed bonus times that dose over the pot size. `ReplantLogic.PickFertilizer` picks the largest such bonus, reading each `SpeedRate` from the planting window, and a tie within 0.0001 goes to the lower `SpeedRate`. The pop text shows only when the containers have no fertilizer, and a seed with `NoBaseFert` (a research crop) gets no fertilizer. Flag a hard-coded fertilizer order or speed value, or a pick that needs a full dose.
- **The research crop comes from the game's own facts.** The mod reads `PlantComponent.NeverWithers()` (the `neverWithers` pot data field), `Data_Web_PlantPanel_Seed.NoBaseFert`, the anomaly bit 256 (Needs Fertilizer), and a game row with `harvestTotalSeconds <= 0` (no harvest window). Flag a copy of the research crop's plant id in the mod.
- **The save stays loadable without the mod.** The pot values go in the game's counter table under `greenline.` keys, which the game ignores. Flag a new save field or a write outside those keys.
- **Page scripts.** The TypeScript modules of `src/Web/page/` (entry `main.ts`, the shared types in `types.ts`) run in the root page with the grid and the pot card in the `CoreUI1` iframe. The modules of `src/Web/plantpanel/` add the pot options to the planting windows. Vite builds each entry into one IIFE file under `obj/page/`, which the csproj target `BuildPage` runs and the DLL embeds as `Greenline.page.js` and `Greenline.plantpanel.js`. The styles are in the `.css` files of `src/Web/`, with the shared values in `tokens.css`. A script writes to the DOM only when a value differs, and it turns off a feature whose page part is missing. At the mod root, `npm test` runs the Vitest page tests of `tests/page` against the game's own pages, `npm run typecheck` checks the types, and `npm run lint` checks the CSS.
- **Mod texts in the i18n files.** Each text of the mod is in `src/i18n/` (`en.json`, `zh.json`, and `text-keys.json`, which maps a text to the game's text key), read through `src/ModTexts.cs` on the library's `GameTexts`, which alone reads the display language and picks the file. The page scripts read each mod text that C# sent through the library's `word` (`src/Shared/i18n/web/`), hold no default text of their own, and draw a part with a mod text only after the first pot data or `setState`. Flag a player text in code (also as a page default), or another read of the display language.
- **No result callbacks.** Each `ExecuteJavaScript` call of the mod passes a `null` callback (a result callback can crash the web UI browser). Each command is a statement that gives no value (`if(window.__greenline)...;else window.vuplex.postMessage('slmod|greenline|no script');`). The page answers only by a page message `slmod|greenline|<text>`: `no script`, `no frame`, `check <result>` (only when not ok), `missing <parts>`, `error <text>`, `plant panel <result>` (only a problem), `counts ...` (Verbose, once each real minute), and `hover error: ...`. `PageMessages` only routes: it sets a request of `PotGrid.Sends` (`SendLogic`) or logs a warning once for each text, and calls no `ExecuteJavaScript` itself; the next `PotGrid.PushIfDirty` sends. Flag a lambda callback (`(Il2CppSystem.Action<string>)(r => ...)`), a command that gives a value C# reads, or an `ExecuteJavaScript` call inside a page message handler.
- **The climate areas are the game's.** The area of a pot is `EnvAreaHelper.GetFurnitureAreaId`, its name `GetAreaDisplayName`, and the line values the HUD's own formula: light `WeatherManager.GetLightValue() x EnvAreaHelper.GetLightMul(area)`, temperature `EnvAreaHelper.GetAreaTemperature(area) - WeatherManager.GetColdValue()`, with `WeatherManager` the instance `BaseSingleton<BattleLogicWorld>.Instance._WeatherManager`. They are read once for each area at each check, in a try block: a failure turns off the zone lines or the values with one warning. Flag a table of area names, light factors, or temperatures in the mod, and a float formatted with the current culture (the game's culture can write a decimal comma).
- **Light load on the web UI.** A push of the pot data sends only `window.__greenline.setPots(json)`; the full page script goes only after the page posts `no script` (a new root page), at most once each 5 real seconds (`SendLogic`). No `install()` after `setPots`: one push is one pass, and a push with no CoreUI1 frame posts `no frame`, so the next check of `PotGrid` pushes again. The area values go into the pot data as formatted texts, so a push happens only when a shown value changes. The pot data has no time to mature for a crop with no problem (`growRemainSeconds` is 0), so it changes only on a real change; `fertDose` (from `PlantFertMissing`) and `neverWithers` change only at a planting; the card reads that time from the game row, and only while the pot data and the row (status 0) both say the crop has no problem. The page updates on a 250 ms `setInterval` step, never a `requestAnimationFrame` loop. Flag a change that sends the script or the data on each check, puts a changing value into the pot data, or adds a per-frame loop.

## Release and config hygiene

- **Verbose ships off.** The `Verbose` config binds with default `false`. Diagnostic tracing goes on `LogDebug` behind it; `LogInfo` stays quiet apart from the load line.
- **The plugin GUID never changes.** It is `com.ivmakk.survivallog.greenline`, the BepInEx identity and the config file name. Flag any edit to it.
- **The version is in two places that must agree:** `<Version>` in the csproj and the `BepInPlugin` attribute.
- **Config docs match the code.** A change to a `Config.Bind` default, name, or effect also changes `CONFIG.md`.
- **No committed build output.** Flag `bin/`, `obj/`, `dist/`, `node_modules/`, or a game DLL in the diff. Game `<Reference>` entries keep `<Private>false</Private>`.
- **Changelog matches the change.** A player-visible change adds an `[Unreleased]` entry to `CHANGELOG.md` in player-facing wording. An internal-only refactor gets none.
